doc: Make and check fighters: hurtboxes baked from the animation, contact sheets, stage pictures, art cut from sheets, the roster's balance.

tools.name: fighter.check
tools.description: Whether each fighter's baked hurtboxes are what its look and moves make now (stale ones name the command that fixes them)

dir.description: a file or directory path: a directory of fighters

tools.name: fighter.bake
tools.description: Bake each fighter's hurtboxes from its look's animation into <name>.boxes.gongfu.toml
tools.undo: the files are derived: restore the previous ones from version control (or bake again from the sources)

dir.description: a file or directory path: a directory of fighters

tools.name: fighter.embed
tools.description: Write the fighters as a module partition for a program; refused while a bake is stale
tools.undo: delete or restore the written file

out.description: a file or directory path: the .cppm written

tools.name: fighter.sheet
tools.description: A contact sheet of a fighter's clips with their boxes, frame by frame, as PNG

out.description: a file or directory path: the PNG written

tools.name: stage.picture
tools.description: A stage as a frame of the game: its layers, two fighters for scale, the camera framing them as the game does

dir.description: a file or directory path: the stages' directory

fighters.description: a fighters' directory and two names: <dir> a,b

tools.name: art.cut
tools.description: Cut a sheet of drawn parts on a flat background into pieces: each keyed out and written as a PNG, listed with its region

sheet.description: a file or directory path: the sheet PNG

out.description: a file or directory path: the directory written

tools.name: art.picture
tools.description: A picture made ready for a look: keyed out, trimmed to what it shows, scaled to a width, written as PNG or WebP

tools.name: roster.versus
tools.description: Bots play every pair of the directory's fighters, sides swapped: wins, damage, supers and round length per pair; each fighter's win rate and where its damage comes from

system.description: a file or directory path: a system file other than the default
